title: Detect, Distill and Update: Learned DB Systems Facing Out of Distribution Data
summary: Proposes DDUp, a framework that decides whether newly inserted rows are out-of-distribution by running a two-sample test on the model's own loss values, then updates the learned component by sequential self-distillation instead of retraining it from scratch. TVAE, the variational autoencoder released alongside CTGAN, is the model the framework is instantiated on for the data-generation task: it is trained, then distilled with a loss the paper defines over the encoder and decoder logits, with the teacher reusing the student's latent noise.
evidence: section 4.3 'Instantiating the Approach': TVAE is used for learned synthetic tabular data generation, and the distillation loss is an average of MSE over the encoder and decoder logits; section 5.1.4 evaluates it by classifier accuracy on generated samples

title: A deep learning anomaly detection framework with explainability and robustness
summary: Presents MAIP, a GUI framework that pairs a stacked-autoencoder and CNN detector for encrypted malicious traffic with SHAP and LIME explanations and a built-in adversarial attack and defence module. CTGAN is the tabular generator behind the framework's GAN poisoning attack, exposed as its own API endpoints, and the rows it produces are also fed back as adversarial training data to answer the paper's robustness question.
evidence: Table 2 lists POST /attacks/ctgan and POST /attacks/poisoning/ctgan among the framework's APIs; section 5.1 threat model states CTGAN is used for modelling tabular data to generate synthetic samples; Figure 4 plots CTGAN output against real data

title: Coherent Multi-Table Data Synthesis for Tabular and Time-Series Data with GANs
summary: Argues that generating tabular and time-series tables independently destroys the links between them, and proposes CMTGAN, which synthesises the main table first and then conditions a new temporal-convolutional time-series GAN on it so the tables stay joinable. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five tabular generators benchmarked on the bank's client-difficulty dataset, and the winner the paper adopts, CTAB-GAN+, carries CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling forward.
evidence: Table 1 reports CTGAN at CMD 0.108, f1 0.593, AUC 0.773 and TVAE alongside it; section 2.2 names CTGAN among the GAN derivatives for tabular data; section 3.1 notes CTAB-GAN+ follows CTGAN in using mode-specific normalization

title: Multi-objective evolutionary GAN for tabular data synthesis
summary: Treats disclosure risk and utility as two conflicting objectives rather than one, evolving a population of generators under NSGA-II with a reinforcement-learning agent choosing which of three loss functions trains each offspring, and adds an Improvement Score to select a final generator before risk climbs. The resulting model, SMOE-CTGAN, keeps CTGAN's backbone, conditional vector, training-by-sampling, Gumbel-softmax and PacGAN discriminator settings unaltered and replaces only the optimisation around them, so it is a named variant built directly on CTGAN.
evidence: section 2.1 states that in the proposed method CTGAN serves as the foundation; section 3 keeps the backbone model structure identical to CTGAN with the conditional vector, Gumbel softmax and PAC settings unaltered; code released at github.com/HuskyNian/SMO_EGAN_pytorch

title: Machine Unlearning in Learned Databases: An Experimental Analysis
summary: First study of data deletion, rather than insertion, in neural-network-backed database components, comparing retraining, fine-tuning, gradient ascent, NegGrad+, SCRUB and SISA across cardinality estimation, approximate query processing, data generation and classification, and proposing model-internal metrics alongside downstream ones. TVAE, released with CTGAN, is the data-generation model being unlearned; its forget quality is measured by the accuracy of an XGBoost classifier trained on samples it generates after deletion, following the protocol of the CTGAN paper.
evidence: section 4.2 names TVAE as the synthetic tabular data generator for the DG task; section 7.1.3 evaluates it through an XGBoost classifier trained on synthetic samples as in the CTGAN paper; Table 4 reports retain and delete f1-scores for TVAE under each unlearning method

title: TRGAN: A Time-Dependent Generative Adversarial Network for Synthetic Transactional Data Generation
summary: Generates synthetic bank transactions with a supervisor-controlled GAN whose conditional vector encodes both client categories and chronology, and draws inter-transaction intervals from Poisson variables with per-client intensities calibrated by optimisation. SDV's RDT transformers do the preprocessing the model depends on, the frequency encoder for high-cardinality client fields and the Gaussian normalizer for numeric ones, and CTGAN and CopulaGAN are two of the three models the result is measured against.
evidence: section 3.2 preprocessing cites docs.sdv.dev/rdt for the frequency encoder applied to client features and the Gaussian normalizer applied to numerical attributes; Tables 1 and 2 compare TRGAN against CTGAN and CopulaGAN on the Czech and UK datasets; the SDV paper is cited as the source of CopulaGAN

title: FLIGAN: Enhancing Federated Learning with Incomplete Data using GAN
summary: Addresses class and volume incompleteness across federated edge nodes by training a per-class-label WGAN-GP without moving raw data, grouping nodes by data volume so sparse groups get fewer rounds, and adding synthetic rows step by step until accuracy stops improving. CTGAN is named as the tabular-GAN prior art the federated design departs from, and the machine-learning-efficacy protocol used to judge the generated data is taken from the CTGAN paper rather than the library being run.
evidence: section 4.2.3 validates the generated datasets using the machine learning efficacy method of reference 16, the CTGAN paper; section 5 and Table 4 list CTGAN as related tabular-GAN work with no privacy preservation; the model itself is WGAN-GP
